visual_goal: Show the resolver reading layered facts and the catalog, asking a purchase gate before buying as-built data, and publishing one resolved view that all products read, with portal mapping at the edge.
prompt: A simple left-to-right diagram with exactly five elements on two rows. Top row, left to right: a three-drawer tray labeled 'Fact store', a gear hub labeled 'Resolver', and a document card labeled 'Resolved view'. Bottom row: a toll-gate barrier labeled 'Purchase gate' directly under 'Resolver', and an open cardboard box labeled 'Build data' directly under 'Fact store'. Exactly four arrows: one from 'Fact store' right into 'Resolver'; one thick arrow from 'Resolver' right into 'Resolved view'; one from 'Resolver' down into 'Purchase gate'; one orange arrow from 'Purchase gate' left into 'Build data', labeled 'buy once'; and one arrow from 'Build data' up into 'Fact store'. To the right of 'Resolved view', three small textless product screens (a gauge, a car advert, a chart) fed by short arrows from 'Resolved view'. No other arrows. No currency symbols, no prices, no percentages.
alt: The fact store feeds the resolver, which publishes one resolved view to products and asks a purchase gate, which buys build data once into the fact store.

visual_goal: Show the specification resolution states, with 'Edition unknown' as a legitimate state with two ways out, and conflicting evidence moving resolved states into a disputed review state.
prompt: A simple state map of six rounded tiles. Left: grey tile 'Candidates'. Middle row center: green tile 'Edition resolved'. Bottom row center: orange tile 'Edition unknown'. Bottom row right: teal tile 'Dealer-confirmed'. Middle row right: dark green tile 'As-built confirmed'. Top row center, above 'Edition resolved': red tile 'Disputed'. Exactly eight solid arrows, each with one arrowhead at its end: 1) from 'Candidates' pointing into 'Edition resolved'; 2) from 'Candidates' pointing into 'Edition unknown'; 3) from 'Edition unknown' pointing up into 'Edition resolved', labeled 'as-built later'; 4) from 'Edition unknown' pointing right into 'Dealer-confirmed', labeled 'dealer answers'; 5) from 'Edition resolved' pointing right into 'As-built confirmed'; 6) from 'Dealer-confirmed' pointing up into 'As-built confirmed'; 7) a red arrow starting at 'As-built confirmed' and pointing up-left into 'Disputed'; 8) a red arrow starting at 'Edition resolved' pointing up into 'Disputed', and next to it a separate blue arrow starting at 'Disputed' pointing down into 'Edition resolved', labeled 'reviewed'. 'Candidates' has only outgoing arrows. There is no arrow between 'Edition unknown' and 'As-built confirmed'.
alt: Candidates lead to Edition resolved or Edition unknown; Edition unknown leaves via a dealer answer or a later as-built purchase; resolved and as-built confirmed states can move into Disputed on conflicting evidence and return after review.

visual_goal: Show the Golf Variant appraisal: free register facts narrow the car to three editions, the value spread of 2,900 EUR justifies one build-data purchase, and the answer comes back as Style with options.
prompt: A left-to-right swimlane illustration with four vertical lanes, each headed by an icon and label: a tablet labeled 'Dealer app', a gear hub labeled 'Specbook', a toll-gate barrier labeled 'Purchase gate', and an open box labeled 'Build data'. Messages flow downward as horizontal arrows. First arrow from 'Dealer app' to 'Specbook' labeled 'plate'. Then, inside the 'Specbook' lane, three small car cards side by side labeled 'Life', 'Style' and 'R-Line', with a bracket under them labeled '€2,900 spread'. Then an arrow from 'Specbook' to 'Purchase gate' labeled 'worth buying?'. Then an arrow from 'Purchase gate' to 'Build data' labeled 'buy once'. Then a return arrow from 'Build data' all the way back to 'Specbook' labeled 'Style + options'. Finally a green return arrow from 'Specbook' to 'Dealer app' labeled 'as-built confirmed'.
alt: Swimlanes for the dealer app, Specbook, the purchase gate and the build-data provider: a plate narrows the car to Life, Style or R-Line with a 2,900 euro spread, the gate buys build data once, and Style with options comes back as as-built confirmed.
